title: Enterprise Vibe Coding: Building Secure, AI-Powered Apps in 30 Minutes - Parth Sharma
summary: OutSystems vendor talk: low-code 'agentic systems engineering' with a context graph, claiming secure apps by default.

assertions.quote: is going to be 100% secure, 100% working 100% of the times

verdicts.note: Platform guardrails can remove classes of bugs (e.g. SQL injection), but no generator makes apps '100% secure'; logic flaws, access-control mistakes and misconfiguration remain.

assertions.quote: How do you go from an idea to production in less than 30 minutes?

verdicts.note: A demo CRUD app can be generated in minutes, but enterprise production also needs requirements, integration, security review and operations; no evidence supports sub-hour delivery as normal.

assertions.quote: teams are shipping code faster than you can actually keep track of

verdicts.note: GitClear and DORA 2025 data show more churn and duplication and lower delivery stability as AI adoption rises; more code means more to maintain.
Smells make up 89% of AI-introduced issues and pass review easily. The paper argues AI's higher speed and volume let these accumulate into a substantial maintenance burden.

assertions.quote: Context gap ... full context of your portfolio

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: Mentor is first going to actually give you a blueprint that you can iterate on

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.
